subject: phys
source: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625) syllabus for examination in 2026, 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Year 11 covers topics 4–6 plus full-course revision for the May/June exams

weeks.topic: Electrical charge and electric fields
objectives: Describe positive and negative charges and forces between them
Explain charging by friction
Describe electric field patterns

weeks.topic: Electric current: conventional current and electron flow
objectives: Define current as rate of flow of charge
Use Q = It
Distinguish conventional current and electron flow

weeks.topic: Electromotive force and potential difference
objectives: Define e.m.f. and potential difference
Measure p.d. with a voltmeter

weeks.topic: Resistance and current–voltage characteristics
objectives: Use R = V/I
Sketch I–V graphs for a resistor, filament lamp and diode

weeks.topic: Resistance of a wire: length and cross-sectional area
objectives: Describe how resistance depends on length and cross-sectional area
Investigate resistance of a wire experimentally

weeks.topic: Electrical energy and power; the kilowatt-hour
objectives: Use P = IV and E = IVt
Calculate the cost of electricity using kWh

weeks.topic: Circuit diagrams and components: thermistors, LDRs and diodes
objectives: Draw and interpret circuit diagrams
Describe the behaviour of thermistors and light-dependent resistors

weeks.topic: Series and parallel circuits
objectives: Calculate current, p.d. and combined resistance in series and parallel circuits
Explain the advantages of parallel lighting circuits

weeks.topic: Potential dividers
objectives: Explain how a potential divider works
Use the ratio of resistances to calculate output voltage
Describe sensor circuits

weeks.topic: Electrical safety: fuses, earthing and circuit breakers
objectives: Identify hazards such as damaged insulation and overloading
Explain the use of fuses, circuit breakers and earthing
Choose an appropriate fuse rating

weeks.topic: Electromagnetic induction
objectives: Describe how an e.m.f. is induced by changing magnetic fields
State the factors affecting the size of induced e.m.f.
Apply Lenz's law

weeks.topic: The a.c. generator
objectives: Describe the structure of a simple a.c. generator
Sketch and interpret output voltage–time graphs

weeks.topic: Magnetic effect of a current; electromagnets and relays
objectives: Describe the field around a wire and a solenoid
Explain how electromagnets and relays work

weeks.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor; Fleming's left-hand rule
objectives: Describe the force on a wire in a magnetic field
Use Fleming's left-hand rule to predict direction
Describe the deflection of charged particle beams

weeks.topic: Review: electrical quantities, circuits and electromagnetism
objectives: Practise circuit calculations
Revise electromagnetic effects and safety

weeks.topic: The d.c. motor
objectives: Explain how a d.c. motor works
Describe the role of the split-ring commutator
Identify ways to increase turning effect

weeks.topic: Transformers and electricity transmission
objectives: Describe the structure of a transformer
Use Vp/Vs = Np/Ns
Explain why high voltages reduce power losses in transmission

weeks.topic: The nuclear model of the atom and nuclide notation
objectives: Describe the structure of the atom
Use nuclide notation for protons and nucleons
Describe the alpha-scattering evidence for the nucleus

weeks.topic: Nuclear fission and fusion
objectives: Describe nuclear fission in reactors
Describe nuclear fusion in stars

weeks.topic: Detection of radioactivity and background radiation
objectives: Describe how a Geiger–Müller tube detects radiation
Identify sources of background radiation
Correct count rates for background

weeks.topic: Alpha, beta and gamma radiation: properties and decay equations
objectives: Compare the penetration and ionising effects of alpha, beta and gamma
Write decay equations
Describe deflection in electric and magnetic fields

weeks.topic: Half-life
objectives: Define half-life
Calculate half-life from data and decay curves

weeks.topic: Safety precautions and uses of radioactivity
objectives: Describe safe handling and storage of radioactive sources
Explain uses in smoke alarms, tracers, sterilisation and thickness control

weeks.topic: Earth and the Solar System: day, seasons, the Moon and orbits
objectives: Explain day and night, seasons and phases of the Moon
Describe the planets and their orbits
Calculate orbital speed using v = 2πr/T

weeks.topic: The Sun as a star and the life cycle of stars
objectives: Describe the Sun as a medium-sized star powered by fusion
Describe the life cycle of stars including supernovae and black holes

weeks.topic: Galaxies, redshift, the Big Bang and the Hubble constant
objectives: Describe galaxies and the Milky Way
Explain redshift as evidence for an expanding Universe
Use the Hubble constant to estimate the age of the Universe

weeks.topic: Mock exams: full syllabus (multiple choice, theory and practical papers)
objectives: Complete full-length mock papers under exam conditions
Use mock feedback to set revision priorities

weeks.topic: Review: motion, forces and momentum
objectives: Revise motion graphs and equations of motion
Practise moments and momentum calculations

weeks.topic: Review: energy, work, power and pressure
objectives: Practise energy and efficiency calculations
Revise energy resources and pressure

weeks.topic: Review: thermal physics
objectives: Revise the particle model and gas laws
Practise specific heat capacity and latent heat questions

weeks.topic: Review: waves, light and sound
objectives: Practise ray diagrams and refraction calculations
Revise the electromagnetic spectrum and sound

weeks.topic: Review: electricity and magnetism
objectives: Practise circuit calculations
Revise motors, generators and transformers

weeks.topic: Review: nuclear and space physics; practical skills
objectives: Revise radioactivity and half-life
Revise space physics
Practise planning experiments and analysing data

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: multiple choice paper (Paper 1 or 2)
objectives: Answer multiple-choice questions efficiently
Check units and use estimation

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: theory paper (Paper 3 or 4)
objectives: Answer structured questions with correct equations and units
Show working clearly

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: practical or alternative to practical paper (Paper 5 or 6)
objectives: Plan experiments and identify variables
Record readings and plot graphs accurately

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: final exam window and course reflection
objectives: Complete any remaining exam papers
Reflect on the course and next steps for IB or A Level Physics
